questions.stem: A rectangle with vertices at (0, 0), (3, 0), (3, 2), and (0, 2) is subjected to a shear transformation. The new coordinates of the vertex (3, 2) are (4, 2). What are the new coordinates of the vertex (0, 0)?
questions.solution: The shear transformation shifts the rectangle horizontally by 1 unit without changing the vertical positions. The new coordinates of (0, 0) are thus (1, 0).
questions.explanation: Shear transformations preserve parallel lines and change only the relative distances between them in a specified direction.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to assume that both horizontal and vertical positions change, but in this case, only the horizontal position changes.

questions.stem: Given a square with vertices at (0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), and (0, 1) that undergoes a shear transformation, the new coordinates of the vertex (1, 1) are (2, 1). What is the new x-coordinate of the vertex (0, 0)?
questions.solution: The shear transformation shifts all points in the square horizontally by 1 unit without changing their vertical positions. The new x-coordinate of (0, 0) is thus 1.
questions.explanation: Shear transformations preserve parallel lines and change only the relative distances between them in a specified direction.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to think that the vertex (0, 0) will not move at all, but it does shift horizontally by the same amount as the other points.

questions.stem: A parallelogram with vertices at (-1, 2), (1, 2), (1, 4), and (-1, 4) is transformed by a shear. The new coordinates of the vertex (1, 4) are (2, 4). What are the new coordinates of the vertex (-1, 2)?
questions.solution: The shear transformation shifts all points in the parallelogram horizontally by 1 unit without changing their vertical positions. The new coordinates of (-1, 2) are thus (-1, 3).
questions.explanation: Shear transformations preserve parallel lines and change only the relative distances between them in a specified direction.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to think that both horizontal and vertical positions change, but in this case, only the horizontal position changes.

questions.stem: The point (3, 5) is subjected to a shear transformation with a factor of -2. What are the new coordinates of the point?
questions.solution: A shear transformation with a factor of -2 shifts the point (3, 5) horizontally by multiplying its x-coordinate by -2 while keeping the vertical position unchanged. The new coordinates are thus (1, 3).
questions.explanation: Shear transformations preserve parallel lines and change only the relative distances between them in a specified direction.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to think that both horizontal and vertical positions change, but with a shear factor, only the horizontal position changes.

questions.stem: The line segment connecting points (1, 2) and (3, 4) is transformed by a shear. The new coordinates of the point (3, 4) are (5, 4). What are the new coordinates of the point (1, 2)?
questions.solution: The shear transformation shifts all points on the line segment horizontally by 2 units without changing their vertical positions. The new coordinates of (1, 2) are thus (3, 2).
questions.explanation: Shear transformations preserve parallel lines and change only the relative distances between them in a specified direction.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to think that both horizontal and vertical positions change, but in this case, only the horizontal position changes.

questions.stem: The triangle with vertices at (0, 0), (2, 0), and (2, 3) undergoes a shear transformation. The new coordinates of the vertex (2, 3) are (4, 3). What is the new y-coordinate of the vertex (0, 0)?
questions.solution: The shear transformation shifts all points in the triangle horizontally by 2 units without changing their vertical positions. The new y-coordinate of (0, 0) remains 0.

questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to think that the vertex (0, 0) will move vertically as well, but it does not; only the horizontal position changes.

questions.stem: The rectangle with vertices at (-2, -1), (-2, 3), (4, 3), and (4, -1) is transformed by a shear. The new coordinates of the vertex (4, 3) are (6, 3). What are the new coordinates of the vertex (-2, -1)?
